opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. As full-time staff, max is write unless role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E003 (Alexandra Johnson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: HR's database (authoritative for employment records) shows E003 is a full-time Analyst. Per policy, full-time employees can have up to write; admin is only permitted if the employee's role owns the system, and Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst. The requested admin level exceeds the maximum allowed (write), so I grant the maximum permitted level: write.

- If contractor: read, or write if advanced training; never admin. Security says basic training, so max read.
